description: crl.rs line 75: if self.now_unix < this_update { return Err(Error::CrlExpired); }. RFC 5280 §6.3.3(a) says thisUpdate must not be in the future; rejecting it is correct per spec. However, clock skew between the CRL issuer and the validator is a real operational concern. The current behavior rejects any CRL whose thisUpdate is even 1 second ahead of now_unix with the misleading CrlExpired error, even though the CRL has not expired. The error variant name is wrong for this case: the CRL is not expired, it is not-yet-valid. This is a correctness issue (wrong error) even if the rejection policy is arguably reasonable.
title: CrlChecker rejects CRLs issued in the future (clock skew)
